title: Two projects, one demanding discipline
description: Explore the measurement question behind ArtiSense and the engineering workflow behind AIFIELD. Their connection is useful for design, but evidence for one does not validate the other.
lead: Explore the measurement question behind ArtiSense and the engineering workflow behind AIFIELD. Their connection is useful for design, but evidence for one does not validate the other.

sections.heading: ArtiSense: optical sensing
body: The proposed system combines illumination, a sample-dependent optical response, detection and interpretation. Photonic glucose sensing is a research example. A device-level measurement and clinical accuracy remain outside the supplied evidence.

sections.heading: AIFIELD: design and simulation
body: The September 2026 materials describe photonic CAD and simulation work, including modes, circuits, fields and thermal effects. A glucose-related chip design is an internal engineering example; it does not establish a fabricated sensor result.

sections.heading: Read the evidence in context
body: Both branches separate what the source material describes from the next tests required. AIFIELD design outputs can inform an ArtiSense concept, but simulation cannot substitute for fabrication, calibration or measurement.
